page: Amazon Web Services c7a.large is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or a GPU, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-core capabilities, with the stress-ng single-core CPU test, Geekbench single-core score, and bzip3 single-threaded decompression all placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core and memory-bound performance show notable tradeoffs. The Geekbench multi-core score, PassMark CPU score, and static web serving throughput fall into the bottom 25%, while the PassMark memory score ranks in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show weak read-only performance, though write performance for large blocks remains in the middle 50%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c7a.large serves as an entry-level dedicated compute option, leveraging high-speed DDR5 memory and dedicated AMD cores without the overhead of larger instances. However, the 4.0 GB memory capacity and lack of local storage limit its utility for memory-intensive or storage-heavy applications. This instance is best suited for single-threaded compute tasks, basic text processing, light web serving, and small-scale LLM inference tasks utilizing small models.
